name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v3415: REG-1142. v3403 taught looked_at, and therefore owes_a_look and therefore the push gate, that a cannot-tell verdict is NOT a look. audit() never learned it, so ONE row was read two ways and I walked into it: read OK, pushed, was refused. MEASURED on v3413: looked_at 0, owes_a_look True, audit looks=1. And the gate refusal message points the reader at --audit, the one screen that disagreed with it. It was THREE surfaces, not one: looks feeds the --audit mark, the --audit headline and the --backlog queue, so a could-not-judge version was invisible in every list that exists to surface it. Fixed once at the classification: such a row now increments its own cannot counter and the --audit line prints cannot-tell=N recorded and NOT a look. Verified 0 disagreements over 1,083 versions. Gate builds its OWN temp ledger with all five row kinds rather than reading the untracked one, which on a runner would be a permanent skip reading as a pass: 8 cases, 2 BASELINEs, 3 RED_PROOFs all PROVEN. Heart row the eye audit agrees with the gate is a corroborator with two independent engines, reach BOUNDED and stated because the full compare is 9,234 ms against a 9,000 ms budget: live OK, 751 ms, 83 versions, 11 could-not-judge rows, 0 disagreements.
